title: Throwback to this review from 2 years ago which I 100% stand by! #bro...
transcript: look I gotta be honest I hate the musical cats and this production is a work of genius before I get to my own like personal take I just wanna take a second to like pile on to the praise and reiterate some points that other people have already brought up because it's all 100% true it's wildly entertaining it's beautifully conceived and yes I would recommend going in with some knowledge of ballroom culture documentary Paris is burning is a great crash course it's also just one of the best documentaries I've ever seen it comes to unconventional musical revivals the ones that really aim to reimagine and reinterpret the original there is a case to be made that this is the best one I've ever seen cause if the aim of a production like this is to bring something new to the table and implement an intentional consistent artistic vision that works with the text instead of against it this production absolutely checks all those boxes and then some and of course the dream scenario is also a revival that improves on the original and if you're like me and you don't like this show then the swing here is pretty unbelievable I mean like the literal distance traveled from negative to positive pretty much unmatched for me and yeah there were still a few moments where I was like oh right this is still cats like I still have to listen to this song that I don't like but in general the way everything was contextualized made it a thousand times more enjoyable for me it's the sort of concept where you can do a lot of the math in your head beforehand you can be like oh right it makes sense because that would connect with that that would parallel that etc but the level of detail and depth that they mind by putting cats and ballroom together is way beyond what I imagined even down to finding like double meanings in words that are already in the script and just imbuing everything with such a sense of history and tradition I'm tempted to just start like listing off all the brilliant little moments they find but I won't do that because I don't want to ruin anyone's sense of discovery if you're going to see it but also because there's so many of them that we would just be here all day I think there's a fair question to be asked about like why are we doing an overlay on a popular musical rather than producing original work about ballroom but two things I'd say about that first of all why not both I'd love to also see an original musical about ballroom in addition to this production but I also think there is something special about the act of reclamation and conversation that's taking place here that is just different from what you'd get with an original work it's this feeling of retracing the uncredited queer influences on the popular canon back to their source not that I can say with any sort of scholarly authority that cats was actually inspired by ballroom culture although after seeing this production it's really kind of hard to feel like it wasn't either way as far as I'm concerned from now on cats is a show about ballroom culture and you really can't convince me otherwise
